code_quality.description: The `Subtract(a, b int) int` function is absent from the diff. This is the primary in-scope deliverable required by all three acceptance criteria (AC1–AC3). The file appears as `?? calc/` (untracked) in git status, but no changes to calc/calc.go appear anywhere in the diff and spec compliance cannot be verified.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Add `func Subtract(a, b int) int { return a - b }` to calc/calc.go and commit the file so it appears in the diff.

code_quality.description: No tests for Subtract are present in the diff. The spec explicitly requires tests in calc/calc_test.go covering AC1 (Subtract(5,3)==2), AC2 (Subtract(0,0)==0), and AC3 (Subtract(3,5)==-2).
code_quality.suggested_fix: Add table-driven or individual test cases for the three acceptance criteria to calc/calc_test.go and commit the file.

code_quality.description: `effectiveStatus` checks `allDone && gates` before returning `ready_for_review`, but `FinalizeStage` (updated in this same diff) checks only the three gate booleans. A run with a failed task from an earlier fix cycle that passes all three gates will be labeled `ready_for_review` by FinalizeStage but `needs_human` in summary.md and review.md written by EvidenceStage.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Remove the `allDone` check from `effectiveStatus` to match FinalizeStage: `if rs.FinalValidationPassed && rs.FinalReviewPassed && rs.FinalAcceptancePassed { return runstore.StatusReadyForReview }`

code_quality.description: The diff contains 1500+ lines of changes to CONTINUE.md, cmd/gromit-next/, internal/next/, contracts/, e2e/, and docs/ — none of which are in-scope for this spec. The Architectural Constraint states all code must stay in the `calc` package.
code_quality.suggested_fix: No action for this spec. These changes belong to a separate branch or commit that should not be bundled with the add-subtract spec implementation.

code_quality.description: The structural `*_test.go` coverage check (iterate `ExpectedTouchedArea`, match `_test.go` suffix, downgrade `ir.Pass`) is copy-pasted in two places: the initial inspect path and the repair retry path. Any future logic change must be applied in both places.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Extract to a helper: `func structuralTestFileCoverage(ir InspectResult, task runstore.Task, filesChanged []string) InspectResult` and call it from both paths.

code_quality.description: `runstore.InvocationRecord` and `evidence.InvocationRecord` are duplicate struct definitions with identical fields. Every new field (e.g. `Provider` added in this diff) requires manual updates in both structs and a corresponding line in the field-by-field conversion loop in evidence.go.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Use `runstore.InvocationRecord` as the canonical type in the evidence bundle, importing it from runstore. The import-cycle concern that motivated duplication can be resolved by moving `evidence.InvocationRecord` into runstore (as was done for this struct) and deleting the duplicate.

code_quality.description: `filterForbiddenFixTasks` detects the test-file constraint by scanning for natural-language substrings ("test file" + "do not modify" / "must not be modified" / "not modify"). Differently phrased constraints are silently missed; task objectives containing those words could produce false positives.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Encode the constraint detection as a typed flag on `RunState` (e.g. `ForbidTestFileModification bool`) set during compile from a structured spec field, and key the filter off that flag rather than substring matching.

code_quality.description: `maxTaskIDInQueue` (taskloop.go, operates on `[]taskEntry`, returns `int`) and `maxTaskID` (plan.go, operates on `[]runstore.Task`, returns `string`) are near-identical functions. Any change to the `t-NNN` ID format must be applied in both places.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Consolidate into a single package-level helper `parseTaskIDNum(id string) (int, bool)` in a shared file (e.g. taskid.go) and use it from both call sites.

code_quality.description: Hardcoded absolute paths `/Users/dabrams/gromit` and `/tmp/gromit-fixtures` make the e2e suite non-portable; it cannot run in CI or on any other machine.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Read paths from environment variables (`GROMIT_REPO_ROOT`, `GROMIT_FIXTURE_BASE`) with documented defaults, and set them in the test helper or a Makefile target.

code_quality.description: `AddInvocation` is mutex-protected but `AddCost` is not, creating an asymmetric thread-safety contract. While current sequential stage execution makes this safe in practice, the inconsistency makes `Budget`'s concurrency guarantees unclear to future maintainers.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Either protect `AddCost` with the same mutex, or add a doc comment to `AddCost` explicitly stating it is not goroutine-safe and must only be called from a single goroutine.

code_quality.description: Two `//nolint:errcheck` directives on the baseline and drain calls to `cfg.DetectFilesChanged` appear without explanatory comments. Readers cannot determine whether ignoring the error is intentional or an oversight.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Add inline comments: `//nolint:errcheck // baseline call: error means no snapshot; delta call will also fail and return empty, which is safe`

code_quality.description: `renumberSubTasks` is a misleading name — the function stamps new IDs onto freshly decomposed sub-tasks starting at a given offset, not renumbers existing tasks in-place. Callers reading the name expect mutation of existing IDs.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Rename to `assignSubTaskIDs(subTasks []runstore.Task, startAt int) []runstore.Task` to make the allocation semantics clear.

code_quality.description: The comment block before `NormalizeNilFields` mixes a CLAUDE.md cross-reference note (`// See CLAUDE.md nil-field normalization...`) with the exported godoc summary line. godoc renders everything before the first blank line as the public API summary, so the internal design note pollutes package documentation.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Move the `// See CLAUDE.md...` note after the godoc summary line, separated by a blank line, or remove it from the exported symbol's comment entirely.
